fix: make a failed generation visible instead of silently resetting (#959)

* fix: apply the deterministic profile to non-gemini-prefixed google models

The pre-v3 gate additionally required a gemini- prefix, so a gemma or learnlm
id got a fully neutral profile while every other gate in the same file keys
only on the v3 boundary and would have applied the deterministic default. The
model listing filters on the models/ prefix and not on family, so those ids do
reach the picker, and before #958 they received the low temperature the
analyze surface needs. The gate is now the exact inversion of the v3 check.

This is the third time an unclassifiable-means-neutral gate cost a
deterministic surface its temperature, after the openai-compatible one in
89435a47, so the doc comment records that the prefix requirement was tried and
dropped and why. That fail-safe is for declining to guess an unknown model's
creative sampling; it was never a reason to let a strict json contract run at
whatever the server defaults to.

Confirmed while here that the v3 check cannot misclassify a gemma id: it
requires the literal prefix before it parses any version digits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: tell the user when a tailored generation fails

The stage is derived as generating, then done if there is output, else
configuring. A failed run leaves both outputs empty, so it fell back to the
wizard, and the file had no reference to the error at all: runTailor wrote it
to the session, the hook returned it, and nothing rendered it. The catch only
logged to the console, so there was no toast either. The result was a
generation that appeared to do nothing, which cost two investigations to
reproduce.

Returning to the wizard is the right behaviour, since the user needs to change
something and try again, but it has to arrive with the reason. The error now
renders below the wizard where the user just clicked Generate, and a toast
fires, matching what the AI Generate wizard already did.

The test drives a real failure through the hook and asserts the rendered text
rather than the store field, because a test that only checked the field was
set would have passed against the broken code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: scale the stream deadline by effort and flag a truncated generation

The 300 second deadline was fixed on both sides and reqwest bounds the whole
request, connect through the last streamed byte, so a generation that
legitimately runs longer was killed mid stream. High effort on a large cloud
model with a full resume and job ad sits squarely in that range, which is the
likely throw behind a failure that then vanished into the silent reset. Both
sides now scale by the request's effort, and the renderer stays the outer
bound so the backend's actionable provider error fires first rather than a
generic timeout.

The tables cannot be shared across the IPC boundary, so a test hardcodes the
backend schedule and asserts the renderer exceeds it at every tier. The tier
order is the vendors', where max sits above xhigh, which reads wrong at a
glance and was inverted here at first: max got a shorter deadline than xhigh,
so the highest effort runs got the tightest bound, which is the exact failure
this exists to prevent. The monotonicity tests listed the tiers in the same
wrong order, so they passed against it; only the value assertions caught it.
Both orders are now pinned with a comment saying why.

finish also consulted the stop reason only when the answer was empty, so a
stream that produced text and then reported length took the success path and a
truncated resume was saved and exported as complete. It still completes and
still keeps the partial text, since that text is worth having, but it now
raises a notification through the existing centre rather than presenting a cut
off document as finished.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: generate the stream deadline schedule from one source

The renderer test hardcoded the backend's baseline and effort multipliers, so
a change to either Rust constant alone would have left it passing while the
renderer timeout began firing before the backend deadline. That is the same
shape as the inversion this branch already fixed, where both monotonicity
tests listed the tiers in the wrong order and passed against it, so this table
has now demonstrably drifted once already.

The baseline and the multipliers live in the shared package and generate into
the rust contract, the way the intent vocabulary already does. Both sides
import the same numbers, gen:ipc:check fails on drift, and the test is left
asserting the one thing that is still a real relationship rather than
re-typing the other side's constants. The tier order prose moves with the
table, since it is the only thing standing between the next editor and the
same inversion.

The gemini test now covers learnlm alongside gemma. It does not restore the
neutrality assertion the review asked for: that contract was removed
deliberately, because it was what withheld a temperature from those models on
a strict json surface.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: redact a generation error before it reaches the screen

Showing the failure reason is the point of this branch, but the raw provider
message was reaching the UI unredacted, and this repo has already leaked a
base_url's query string auth into an error that way. The existing redactor was
wired into crash reporting and the diagnostics zip and never into the AI path.

The review asked for a fixed string with the real text kept in the console.
That would undo the change: the user was getting nothing, which is what made a
real failure take two investigations to reproduce, and a generic failed is
barely better than the silent reset it replaced. Redacting at the boundary
keeps both properties, so the reason survives and credentials, paths, hosts
and emails do not.

emit_stream_error is the single choke point. Neither generate command lets the
invoke itself reject; both route their error branch through it, and every
other renderer failure path already uses a fixed string. A test pins that an
ordinary provider error such as 429 Too Many Requests passes through byte for
byte, so the next person cannot answer this by flattening everything and
calling it security.

fix: stop the resume prompt licensing invented metrics, and let each provider own its sampling (#958)

* fix: stop the resume prompt licensing invented metrics

The full-tier resume prompt said never fabricate numbers, only use metrics if
they are in the original OR CAN BE REASONABLY INFERRED, two lines after
demanding every bullet carry a measurable result, and ats mode adds quantify
every achievement. Three other rules in the same prompt ban exactly what that
clause permits. The brief tier and the Rust port of the same spine both get it
right, so the full tier, the one cloud users hit, was the outlier. A resume
with an invented number is one the candidate has to defend in an interview.

The analyze prompt fought itself the same way: synonyms fail 70% of the time
and hard skills must match EXACTLY, then a hundred and fifty lines later
React.js equals React equals ReactJS, while the user prompt and the Rust
synonym map both implement semantic matching. That decides missingKeywords and
keywordCoverage, which the user sees. The ATS score was also decomposed two
incompatible ways in one system prompt.

Also removes about five hundred tokens instructing a weighted overall score
that has no field in the schema, a dangling CANDIDATE RESUME header emitted
after the resume it announces, a leaked topRequirements variable name, and a
duplicate point budget. The German subject label now goes through the output
language fitter like the salutation and sign-off already did, the format
skeleton gains the subject slot it mandates, and the company research sentences
are gated on a brief actually being fenced.

Prompt size was measured, not assumed: resume 4563 tokens, analyze 5684. Size
was never the problem and nothing was rewritten for it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: let each provider own its sampling values instead of the renderer

The renderer picked a temperature per task step and sent it to whatever model
happened to be configured. That is wrong on most of them now. Non-default
temperature, top_p or top_k returns 400 on every request to Claude 4.7 and
later, thinking or not. OpenAI reasoning models reject temperature. Google says
to remove the parameters from Gemini 3 requests entirely and documents that a
temperature below 1.0 causes looping. Six of eight families publish one number
per model with no task dimension at all, so the per-step table was tuning an
axis no vendor supports.

Gemini already had a guard for this and it was dead code. It withheld the
adapter's own fallback only when the caller supplied nothing, but the renderer
always supplied something, so every request looked like a deliberate user
choice. The onboarding default is a Gemini 3 model, so new users hit the
documented degradation case on their first generation.

The renderer now sends an intent and each adapter owns the numbers, behind a
trait method whose default sends nothing at all. Omitting is correct or better
on Claude, OpenAI reasoning models, Gemini 3, native Ollama, which inherits the
modelfile, and vLLM gateways, which inherit generation_config. An unknown model
on an unknown provider therefore falls through to that provider's own defaults,
so a new model still needs no code. Anthropic needed no change: its fail-safe
was already right, and the work was generalising it to the other four adapters.

Explicit values still win, so the per-model temperature sliders keep working.
prose_grounded keeps presence_penalty off the surfaces that write factual
claims about the candidate to a third party, since that penalty pushes toward
new topics. Ollama Cloud is special-cased because its openai-compatible layer
hardcodes 1.0 when a value is omitted, overriding the modelfile.

Also routes the job analysis and the inline rewrite through the resolver. Both
used bare literals, so the analysis slider changed metadata extraction and not
the analysis it is named for.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep the deterministic sampling the providers actually accept

The first cut of this change defaulted every adapter to sending nothing, on
the theory that omitting a value is neutral. It is not. Omitting means the
model applies its own default, which is 0.7 to 1.0, so the analyze surface
went from 0.1 to 1.0 on most providers while its prompt is a strict JSON
contract that hard-throws on a parse failure, and the grounded prose surfaces
went from 0.5 to 1.0 while their whole purpose is staying traceable to the
resume. Measured on this machine, the local models carry temperature 1 and
presence_penalty 1.5 in their own modelfiles, so on the default install the
resume surface would have run hotter and with the exact penalty that pushes a
model toward inventing facts.

Omission is right only where sending is refused or documented as harmful:
Claude 4.7 and later, OpenAI reasoning models, Gemini 3, and any model an
adapter cannot classify. Everywhere else each adapter now declares the values
that reproduce today's behaviour. Anthropic and Ollama were reading the
request directly and never consulted their own profile, which is what kept
Anthropic's hardcoded fallback invisible; both now resolve through it.

The cover letter moves to the grounded profile. Calling it creative was an
argument about temperature, not about a penalty that rewards new topics in a
letter asserting real achievements to an employer. Inline rewrite goes back to
deterministic, since a span edit should not inherit a prose profile. The
openai-compatible adapter no longer hands OpenAI's numbers to arbitrary
gateways.

Tests now assert the request body per adapter and per intent, including the
absences, because the previous round asserted the intent string and every one
of these defects passed. The intent vocabulary is generated from the shared
schema so a renamed literal cannot silently degrade every request to the
default. Settings no longer claims app defaults apply when the modelfile does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* build: track the generated ai intents contract

pub mod ai_intents in ipc_contracts/mod.rs referenced a file that was never
added, so the crate compiled here and would not on a fresh checkout. Staging
by path rather than wholesale is the right habit, but it does not pick up a
new file on its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: gate the technology requirement on the resume actually naming one

The bullet formula was fixed for metrics and left mandatory for technology in
the same line, so a bullet whose original names no tool, mentored three junior
engineers, still had to name one. That is the fabrication class this branch
exists to close, one token to the left of where it was closed. Now conditional
at all five sites, including a task-tier copy nobody had listed, with wording
shared so they cannot drift apart again, and the duplicate formula line is
gone.

One temperature slider was driving three intents. The answers key covered
application answers, the job ad summary and every interview surface, so
enabling it retuned deterministic summarisation and prose questions too. Each
key now maps to exactly one intent, with a new questions key, and the tests
assert that a sibling override does not leak, which is what would have caught
it. Slider labels name the surfaces they affect and the automatic mode copy no
longer promises modelfile behaviour that only some providers get.

The grounded prose temperature is higher than the ungrounded one, which reads
backwards, so its doc comment now explains that grounding comes from
withholding presence_penalty rather than from cooling the sampler, and that the
ordering is an accident of which surfaces carry which intent. The test that
claimed the opposite is renamed.

API.md documented a GenerateRequest that does not exist, with fields the real
schema never had, and returned a generationId where the contract returns a
jobId. Replaced with a pointer to the schema that owns it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep the deterministic temperature on openai-compatible gateways

Last round I told the author to gate the openai profile on the native provider
id, after a reviewer objected that handing our numbers to arbitrary gateways
contradicted the unknown-model fail-safe. That over-corrected. LM Studio,
vLLM, OpenRouter and any custom endpoint fell to a fully neutral profile, so
the analyze surface lost the low temperature it had before this branch, on a
prompt that is a strict JSON contract and a caller that throws on a parse
failure.

The distinction I missed is that deterministic encodes an app requirement, not
a model preference. The fail-safe is about not guessing what creative sampling
an unknown model wants; it was never a reason to let a JSON contract run hot.
Compatible gateways now resolve the same profile as native OpenAI, behind the
same unchanged reasoning-model gate, and the doc comment records that the id
gate was tried and reverted so the objection does not get re-raised and
flipped back.

Also covers generateReferralImprove, which changed intent alongside its
sibling and had no test.

fix: stop the resume header rendering twice and repair pre-v0.134.0 link mojibake (#957)

* docs: add the landing workspace to the monorepo directory listings

apps/landing has been a real pnpm workspace for a while but appeared in none
of the four Markdown listings that describe the tree, so every one of them
told a reader the repo has two apps.

docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's block was the stalest: it still called the desktop app
apps/tauri, pointed at a src/tauri-client.ts that is a directory, and omitted
apps/extension and packages/translations as well.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: reconcile the resume header name in place instead of stacking a second one

seedHeaderFromProfile only recognised the document's own name line when it sat
at exactly index 0. Two shapes defeated that. An ALL-CAPS name passes
isAllCapsSectionHeading, so looksLikeHeaderBoundary read it as a section
heading and the profile's name was unshifted above it; and a leading blank
line, which PDF extraction routinely emits, pushed the real name line to
index 1 where nothing looked for it. Either way the contact scan then broke on
that same line at i = 1, found no match, and spliced a second contact line in
too, so the export rendered the whole header twice: the styled header, then a
body section headed with the ALL-CAPS name carrying the title and the original
contact line.

The header block is now searched for a line that already IS the profile's name,
compared casing- and punctuation-insensitively, and that one line is
overwritten in place. It is the only safe re-scoping of a line the boundary
predicate flagged, because it can match nothing except the name we are about to
write there; every other line keeps the never-remove-or-blind-overwrite
invariant from #931.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: key the resume name rule on the first line with content, not raw line 0

parse_line decided "this line is the candidate's name" from the raw line
index. PDF extraction routinely emits a leading blank line before the header
text, so the real name landed at index 1, missed the rule, matched
is_all_caps_section_heading instead, and became a section header. That flips
seen_section immediately, so the title and contact lines below were swallowed
into a section named after the candidate while header.name and header.contact
stayed empty and apply_to_header refilled them from the contact profile — the
header rendered twice, once styled and once as a body section.

idx == 0 is kept as its own arm so the original rule cannot regress whatever
all_lines holds; past that the preceding lines must all be blank and idx must
be a real index into all_lines, since an out-of-bounds range must not read as
a vacuously-true empty slice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: match accented and all-caps names when reconciling the resume header

Three defects the sibling review caught in the name reconciliation.

nameKey claimed NFKD folds accented variants together, and it does not. NFKD
splits a composed character into base plus combining mark, the mark is
category Mn rather than a letter or number, so the punctuation collapse turned
it into a space: Francois became "franc ois" and stopped matching FRANCOIS.
Every user whose profile name and resume differ in accent presence fell
through to the old path and got the duplicated header this change exists to
prevent. Combining marks are now stripped outright.

sanitizeHeaderName never changes case, so an all-caps fullName in the profile
left the reconciled line all-caps, the contact scan re-tripped the boundary
predicate on it, broke early, and inserted a second contact line. That index is
now skipped by the scan exactly as index 0 already was. The name keeps the
casing the user typed.

headerBlockEnd spans the whole document when it contains no blank line at all,
so findNameLine could reconcile an occurrence of the name in the body and leave
the header with no name at all. It now stops at the first section boundary,
testing for a name match first so an all-caps name still matches itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: repair pdf link anchors corrupted before the utf-16 decoder landed

pdf_text_string in #955 stopped new corruption but could not touch text
already written. A PDF text string is UTF-16BE behind a FE FF BOM, and reading
it with from_utf8_lossy rendered the BOM as two U+FFFD followed by every
character interleaved with its NUL high byte, so stored link anchors read as
mojibake and matched no project title, leaving every link heaped at the end of
the section instead of on its own entry.

The shape is losslessly reversible, so repair_utf16_mojibake drops the doubled
replacement chars and the NULs, gated on the string containing a NUL at all,
which is never legitimate in stored document text. Two appended migrations
rewrite only NUL-bearing rows in documents.text and in ai_generations'
resume_text and cover_letter_text. A per-row failure warns rather than
propagating: rolling back would undo every other row's repair and leave
user_version wedged, retrying the same failure on every future startup.

Also fixes two pre-existing tests that identified their target as
MIGRATIONS.len() - 1. Appending anything silently pointed them at the wrong
migration, which is the trap a position-indexed list sets for every future
append.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: scope the mojibake repair to the shape it can actually reconstruct

Review round on the repair migrations.

The per-row UPDATE error is propagated instead of swallowed. Swallowing did
not do what its comment claimed: on a disk-full or IO error SQLite auto-rolls
back the enclosing transaction, so the loop continued in autocommit and the
following PRAGMA user_version committed on its own, durably marking the
migration applied while the row stayed corrupt and was never retried. Store
opens are already non-fatal in lib.rs, so propagating costs a session, not the
app.

The repair is now anchored on the corruption's own shape rather than stripping
every doubled replacement char and every NUL in the row. It requires the BOM
marker followed by a NUL, then consumes only (NUL, ASCII) pairs it can
reconstruct. A resume body carrying two adjacent unmapped-glyph markers no
longer has them silently deleted, which fused words on the html and rtf import
paths, and a UTF-16 anchor with non-ASCII code units is left alone rather than
turned into plausible garbage with its markers erased, since those bytes are
still a faithful image of the payload and remain recoverable.

Repaired documents also clear keywords_json and indexed. Rewriting the text
while leaving the cached keywords and the embedding pinned to the corrupt
version would have scored the resume forever against text it no longer
contains. Both migrations snapshot the affected rows first, and the insert,
update and import paths repair on write, so restoring a bundle exported before
this fix cannot re-inject the corruption.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: correct adr-0021 for the in-place header name reconciliation

The decision and consequences both still said seedHeaderFromProfile replaces
line 0. It now searches the header block for the line that already is the
profile's name and overwrites that one in place, falling back to the original
replace-or-insert only when nothing matches. Records the ceiling too: an
all-caps name that does not match the profile still stacks, deliberately,
because guessing would risk destroying a real section heading.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style: apply cargo fmt to the header and mojibake changes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: drop the mojibake snapshot tables on a full data erasure

The repair migrations snapshot every affected row's pre-repair text as a
safety net for an in-place rewrite, and that snapshot holds the user's
original resume and cover letter in plaintext. Neither store's clear_all
knew about it, so a full erase-my-data reset left those documents on disk.
For a local-first app whose privacy story is that documents never leave the
machine and can be erased on demand, that is the wrong outcome, and it exists
only because the snapshot was added.

Both clear_all batches now drop the snapshot alongside the live tables. DROP
rather than DELETE: it is a one-shot migration artifact and user_version is
already past the migration, so nothing recreates it. The tests assert it is
gone from sqlite_master rather than merely empty.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: start the header block at the first content line, not line 1

headerBlockEnd scanned for the terminating blank from index 1, so two or more
leading blank lines made it return 1. findNameLine could then only look at
index 0, never reached the real name, and the seeder fell back to replacing
line 0 and left the original name below it, reproducing the duplicated header
this branch exists to remove.

It also diverged from the parser fix on this same branch, which accepts the
first line with content after any number of leading blanks, so the two halves
of one fix disagreed about where the header starts.

The block is now the first run of content lines. The no-match insert branch
was anchored on line 0 for the same reason and would have spliced the contact
line into a run of blanks, so it follows the same content start. Both reduce
to the previous expressions when nothing leads the text.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: assert the unmappable row survives and collapse the duplicated fixture

The skip-an-unmappable-row test was named for the row being logged and skipped
rather than silently dropped, but asserted only on the mappable row and on
user_version, so a change that deleted the row would still have passed. It now
counts the row directly, since store.get cannot read it at all: its text column
is BLOB storage class, which is what makes it unmappable in the first place.

Five copies of the same corrupt-byte builder and its expected output collapse
into the helper pair ai_generations' tests already use. The large-payload
builder in the failed-write test stays inline: it needs a much bigger payload
to force the failure, so folding it in would lose what that test is for.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: point at the header seeder instead of restating how it works

Both passages had restated seedHeaderFromProfile's matching and scan mechanics,
and had already drifted in the round that wrote them: they described the name
comparison as casing and punctuation insensitive while nameKey also folds
diacritics, which is precisely the case that was broken. The ownership
decision, the never-remove-or-blind-overwrite invariant and the accepted
ceiling stay, since those are the decision; the mechanics now point at the
function that holds them. The landing bullet drops the framework version and
export mode for the same reason.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep the first content line out of the contact overwrite scan

Index 0 was excluded from the scan because a combined first line such as
Jane Doe | jane@example.com has no separate name line, so overwriting it
erases the name outright. Moving the header block start to the first content
line left that exclusion pinned to index 0, so behind two or more leading
blanks the line it was written to protect became a candidate again and was
blind-overwritten.

The scan now skips the first content line the same way it skips the
reconciled name index. The two usually coincide but not always, so both are
checked independently.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: evict the embedding derived from the corrupt text, not just the flag

The repair set indexed = 0 to force a re-embed, but nothing reads that column
when deciding what to re-embed. stale_documents asks only whether a vector
exists in the active embedding space, so a repaired document kept its old
vector, that vector still matched, and the embedding stayed derived from text
the document no longer contains. The flag was the wrong lever and it was mine.

The migration now deletes the vectors row for every id it repairs, which is
what actually makes the document stale, and the comment names stale_documents
as the consumer so the next reader does not repeat it. insert does the same
when the repair actually changed the text, and import skips restoring the
bundle's own vector in that case rather than cleaning up after it, since the
restore would otherwise land after the delete. A document whose text was
untouched keeps its embedding.

ui: explain what the job match and trust badges mean on hover (#956)

* ui: explain what the job match and trust badges mean on hover

Both badges showed a verdict with no way to learn what it meant. MatchBand
rendered the bare word "High" with no description at all on the Autopilot card;
the jobs list did have a popover, but its copy is a disclaimer ("not the
employer's decision") that never said what the tier itself means. TrustBadge
listed which checks failed ("Suspicious domain") but never the verdict, which
is what tells a reader whether to skip a posting or just look twice.

MatchBand now carries a plain-language description as a native `title` plus an
sr-only suffix, and TrustBadge leads its tooltip with the level's meaning before
the failed-check list.

Deliberately NOT a HoverPopover on MatchBand, despite that being the richer
control TrustBadge uses: the band renders inside a <Button> on the Autopilot
card, where a focusable trigger is invalid button-in-button HTML, and inside
aria-activedescendant listbox rows, where it would add a tab stop per row. Both
constraints are already documented at those call sites. `title` is hover-capable
and focusable-free, so it is safe in both. RowMatchScore, which owns a real
popover already, opts out via describe={false} and folds the tier sentence into
its own copy so a browser tooltip doesn't fire alongside it.

Descriptions are per-VARIANT, not per-tier alone. A coverage High is keyword
overlap with no AI scoring behind it; a combined High blends meaning and
keywords. One shared sentence would have to be vague enough to be true of both.

TrustBadge's detail block was gated on the flag list being non-empty, so a
flagged-but-reasonless assessment rendered a bare badge with nothing to explain
it. Now gated on `interactive` alone — the level description always exists.

Testing note: match-band.test.tsx stubs `t` to echo raw keys, so it structurally
cannot catch a missing translation, and the key is built at runtime from tier +
variant so TypeScript cannot either. Added match-band.i18n.test.tsx using real
translations, matching trust-badge.test.tsx's existing rationale. Verified both
guards fail when a key is deleted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: assert the trust-level description itself, not just the absence of raw keys

CodeRabbit was right and the finding was worse than Minor. The tests asserted
that `detail` contained no raw i18n keys and that the flag list appeared past

fix: pay off three deferred correctness defects (#946)

* fix: key cached match scores on the embedding vector version

Cached semantic scores are computed from embeddings, but the cache key
carried provider, model and formula version — not the vector format. A
format change therefore left every stored score a valid hit against vectors
that no longer mean the same thing.

It has been harmless only by coincidence: the format bump in #933 happened to
land with a MATCH_FORMULA_VERSION bump, and that field IS in the key, so the
scores were invalidated by the formula axis rather than by anything reasoning
about vectors. The next format bump without a coincidental formula bump would
have served stale scores as fresh, silently.

The version is now part of the key and of the table's primary key, so a
format change invalidates by construction. Adding an eviction to each future
migration would have been the patch-the-instance answer, and it depends on
whoever writes the next migration remembering — which is the failure this
already survived once by luck.

Every construction site is exhaustive over the struct, so a new one cannot
omit it.

Found alongside: `posting_vectors` has no persisted version column at all and
synthesizes the current one on read, so it cannot self-detect staleness and
still depends on a hand-written eviction per bump. Left alone — that is a
schema change, not this fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep a stored cookie's domain scope when rebuilding the jar

Cookies were rebuilt for the reqwest jar as `name=value; Path=...` with no
`Domain`, then added against a URL built from the stored domain with its
leading dot stripped. Per RFC 6265 a cookie with no `Domain` attribute is
host-only, so the leading dot — the very thing marking it as applying to
subdomains — was discarded, and a session captured for `.linkedin.com`
stopped reaching `www.linkedin.com`.

The user-visible effect was that whether a request was authenticated depended
on how the URL happened to be spelled, since both forms pass `detect_platform`.

A stored domain carrying the leading dot now rebuilds with `Domain`, and one
without it stays host-only, matching how it was captured.

Deliberately narrow: `Domain` is only ever the cookie's own stored host, never
anything wider. Widening a session cookie's scope would send a credential to a
host it was never issued for, which is worse than the bug being fixed — so
where the stored shape is ambiguous it stays host-only. `Secure` and
`HttpOnly` were already preserved.

The jar-building loop is extracted so it can be asserted against directly,
`reqwest::Client` not exposing its jar after build. The test that matters is
the safety one — a cookie is never attached to an unrelated host — and it was
confirmed load-bearing by temporarily broadening the code and watching it fail.
